scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 Serial2/0 (eth2), 20.20.0.0/8 link
Mechanism: router1 ↔ router2 over the 20.20.0.0/8 serial is
  the only path connecting routers 0/1's subnets to router2's
  Server Room + Internet Lab. With the link down, RIP on both
  sides ages out the unreachable prefixes and connectivity
  splits into two islands (router0+router1 side / router2 side).
Localization: router2 eth2 (or router1 eth3)
Root cause: WAN link router1<->router2 (20.20.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 up` on router2

agent.diagnosis_text:
The WAN interface eth2 on router2 (the wan_r1_r2 segment, IP 20.20.0.2/8) has
been brought down — its kernel flags show <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP or
LOWER_UP, meaning the interface is administratively down. Router1's eth3 (the
other end at 20.20.0.1/8) is fully operational, but its ARP entry for 20.20.0.2
is in state FAILED, confirming that no L2 frames can reach router2 across the
WAN link.

Because router2's eth2 is down, FRR cannot form a RIP adjacency over that
interface. Router2 therefore has no routing-table entry for any network behind
router1 (192.168.1–4.x, 10.x, the IT LAN, the CS LAN, the Office LAN, or the
Principle Room LAN). Conversely, router2 cannot send RIP updates out eth2, so
router1 holds only stale RIP routes to 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16 (learned
before the link went down and not yet expired at 180 s). When hosts on any of
those source networks try to reach the Server Room or Internet Lab, their
packets reach router1, which forwards toward 20.20.0.2, ARP fails, and an ICMP
"Destination Host Unreachable" is returned to the sender. Traffic between the
Server Room (1.0.0.x) and Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) works because both are
locally connected to router2's eth0/eth1 which remain up.

Root cause: router2's eth2 interface has been taken down (equivalent to
`ip link set eth2 down`), severing the sole WAN path between router2 and the
rest of the campus.

Corrective fix: on router2, run `ip link set eth2 up`. RIP will re-establish
the adjacency over the 20.0.0.0/8 link within one update interval (~30 s) and
full reachability will be restored across all campus segments.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the WAN link between router1 (eth3 20.20.0.1/8) and router2 (eth2 20.20.0.2/8 / 20.20.0.0/8) as the affected link.

The writeup explicitly explains the network splitting into two islands (router0/1 side vs router2 side) and ties that symptom to the WAN link being administratively down on router2, clearly distinguishing symptom from root cause.
Corrective action explicitly states to bring up router2's eth2 with 'ip link set eth2 up', which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log contains direct observations (ip link state, neighbor ARP FAILED, routing/ping failures) that support the conclusion; the agent's inferences about RIP adjacency loss and split islands follow logically and the checks cover the essential alternatives. Minor truncations in some command outputs slightly reduce explicit grounding but do not undermine the diagnosis.
